S4.old: An East German 10 pfennig from 1968, feather-light aluminium. One side carries the state emblem, a hammer and compass inside a wreath of wheat, ringed by the words Deutsche Demokratische Republik; the other has a big 10 over an oak leaf. Coins like this were the small change of the DDR until the state itself vanished in 1990.

S5.old: A South Korean 10 won from 2001, struck in brass. The Dabotap pagoda of Bulguksa temple stands on one side, a stone pagoda from the 700s and one of Korea's national treasures, with the value in Hangul beside it. The other side carries a big 10, the year, and the Bank of Korea's name. This brass design ran from 1983 to 2006, when a smaller, cheaper copper-colored version took its place; the collection already holds that successor.
